questions.question: Which formation keeps riders closest together as a group?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps a group close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle for a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes your motorcycle take longer to accelerate and stop.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
Is only useful in protecting riders from dirt.
Does not offer as much protection as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no lane position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that fits your riding conditions.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that go above the ankle
Hearing protection
Pants made of a soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of a soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection with your helmet.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure in saddlebags. Do not pile loads on a sissy bar because it raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Spread loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers can't see you.
Not be concerned with making other drivers see you.
Ride offensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers can't see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers cannot see you.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up, if possible.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down before hitting an obstacle. Approach at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before contact, roll off the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Engine braking:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is slowing down by turning the engine off.
Is slowing down by downshifting.
Is not encouraged because of the damage it does to the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows down your motorcycle in a way similar to braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Where is the electric starter button usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
By the left footrest
By the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The electric starter button is usually located near the right handgrip.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. You are more likely to notice a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol consumption is:

options.text: Better riding abilities
Slowing down of body functions
More nervousness
More alertness

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down of body functions
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic begins to move
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly
Weave between the cars to pass quickly
Not weave between the cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between the cars
questions.explanation: Weaving between parked or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors may open, or cars may pull into traffic. You will not have room to escape. Never ride on the shoulder—other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: Once a motorcycle helmet has been involved in a crash, it should be:

options.text: Inspected closely
Replaced
Sold to another rider
Outfitted with a new chinstrap

questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced
questions.explanation: Replace your helmet after any crash.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: Use the rear brake first
Use the front brake first
Use both brakes at the same time
Use only one brake, front or rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than a car's
A motorcycle's visibility is less important than a car's
Passing should be done on the shoulder, not the main road
You must make eye contact with the other driver

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than a car's
questions.explanation: Visibility is more critical when riding a motorcycle. Your motorcycle is smaller and can easily hide in another vehicle's blind spot. Other drivers may not see you even if they look.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated
Has a seat even with the rider's waist
Has a seat 10 inches above the rider's waist
Has a seat 10 inches below the rider's waist

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets your feet reach the ground while you are seated. Keep your feet on the footrests when riding.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely
Secure the load so it does not shift
Place the load unsecured in the seat
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift
questions.explanation: Secure your load so it cannot shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.
